A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework and retain matching methods, datasets, and experiments. All pages, including appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: Sections 4.3–4.5 and Tables 1–5 report original fine-tuning, codebook-refinement, inter-rater agreement, and ablation results.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by a ratings-only training control, additional model evaluations, and sampling and trace-quantity analyses.

M1.justification: The rejection-sampling procedure, first-matching-trace selection, SFT objective, and two-stage instruction/rubric refinement remain unchanged. The post hoc explanation alternative already appears in v1. Additional model evaluations do not document a new algorithmic procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five datasets and eight rating dimensions: HANNA stories, student essays, SummEval summaries, Chinese-to-English WMT translations, and HelpSteer2 responses. The additions vary models and trace budgets within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 adds a ratings-only SFT comparator, addressing an important alternative to trace-augmented training absent from v1. Appendix Tables 9–10 also add GPT-4o-generated trace variants alongside the existing DeepSeek and gpt-oss variants in both application comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands experimental conditions through a DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B base model, ratings-only training, GPT-4o trace generation, sampling coverage at k values from 1 to 32, and four instruction/rubric trace-budget combinations. The original filtering, metrics, early stopping, LoRA settings, and main k=16 configuration remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds an ablation testing whether traces contribute beyond SFT alone (Table 4), sampling-coverage analysis (Figure 5), and trace-quantity sensitivity analysis (Table 8). Appendix A additionally examines architecture generalization and the need for specialized reasoning generators. The original refinement-component and post hoc ablations remain as Tables 5–6.

E5.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same paired t-tests, one-sided bootstrap tests, and significance reporting. V2 adds no run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures; additional significance-marked results follow the existing practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and significance markers in v1 Tables 1–5 remain in v2 Tables 1–3 and 5–6 after matching metric order. Substantial new results include ratings-only SFT averaging tau=0.191 versus 0.281 with DeepSeek traces, Llama-based SFT increasing average tau from 0.151 to 0.216, and GPT-4o trace variants averaging 0.237 for SFT and 0.339 for codebook refinement. Figure 5 and Table 8 add utilization and sensitivity findings.

T1.justification: The definitions of latent and reconstructed traces, label-matching filter, augmented dataset, and SFT loss in Equation 1 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations absent from the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: reconstructing useful thinking-trace proxies, improving open-model raters through SFT, and refining codebooks to improve human alignment and cross-model agreement. The added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies the shared-bias explanation for reduced inter-rater agreement as a hypothesis rather than asserting bias reduction. It also adds interpretations about the necessity of traces, architecture generalization, generalist generators, and data efficiency. The substantive limitations and future directions in Section 5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The supplied SFT hyperparameters, refinement prompts, and dataset-processing details are retained. Codebook access instructions change from the GitHub repository in v1 Appendix D to an anonymous repository's codebook directory in v2 Appendix E, while the main GitHub reference remains. This establishes changed access instructions, not verified resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds reasoning-distillation references covering medical questions, software engineering, finance, cybersecurity, and general-purpose trace datasets such as Synthetic-1 and OpenThoughts. This locally broadens the literature discussion while retaining the same positioning of codebook refinement as the distinctive second application.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 makes localized explanatory edits, inserts a new SFT-ablation paragraph and an additional-results appendix, adds acknowledgments, and removes the placeholder CCS text. Existing appendix content moves from A–D to B–E without substantial rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column draft layout with a single-column publication layout, redraws Figure 3 with concrete examples, adds the sampling plot and five tables, and reorders metric columns. New Figure 6 visualizes the unchanged Table 3 results. Figures, codebook examples, and prompt boxes are extensively resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added ratings-only SFT control addresses an important missing comparison in v1, substantially strengthening evidence that thinking traces contribute beyond generic fine-tuning. Architecture, generator, and sensitivity experiments further strengthen validation while preserving the original results. Some new appendix wording is imprecise: Table 8 shows a nonmonotonic trace-quantity trend, and Table 9 evaluates GPT-4o-generated traces in a Qwen-based rater despite wording suggesting GPT-4o itself is fine-tuned. These limitations temper individual interpretations but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support.
